officialTitle: Nivolumab versus placebo in patients with relapsed malignant mesothelioma (CONFIRM): a multicentre, double-blind, randomised, phase 3 trial

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Between May 10, 2017, and March 30, 2020, 332 patients were recruited, of whom 221 (67%) were randomly assigned to the nivolumab group and 111 (33%) were assigned to the placebo group).
design.notes: 2:1 randomisation at 24 UK hospitals; stratified by epithelioid vs non-epithelioid histology. Pleural or peritoneal mesothelioma eligible.

sponsor: Stand Up To Cancer-Cancer Research UK and Bristol Myers Squibb
clinicalQuestion: Does nivolumab improve survival over placebo in mesothelioma that has progressed after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy?

pico.population: Pleural or peritoneal mesothelioma with progression after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy, ECOG PS 0-1
pico.intervention: Nivolumab 240 mg every 2 weeks for up to 12 months
pico.outcomes: Co-primary: investigator-assessed PFS and OS. Safety

arms.label: Nivolumab
arms.dosing: 240 mg flat dose IV every 2 weeks until progression or a maximum of 12 months
arms.doseSourceQuote: were randomly assigned (2:1) to receive nivolumab at a flat dose of 240 mg every 2 weeks over 30 min intravenously or placebo until disease progression or a maximum of 12 months.

publications.title: Nivolumab versus placebo in patients with relapsed malignant mesothelioma (CONFIRM): a multicentre, double-blind, randomised, phase 3 trial.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Median progression-free survival was 3·0 months (95% CI 2·8-4·1) in the nivolumab group versus 1·8 months (1·4-2·6) in the placebo group (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0·67 [95% CI 0·53-0·85; p=0·0012).
Median overall survival was 10·2 months (95% CI 8·5-12·1) in the nivolumab group versus 6·9 months (5·0-8·0) in the placebo group (adjusted HR 0·69 [95% CI 0·52-0·91]; p=0·0090).

safety.sourceQuote: Serious adverse events occurred in 90 (41%) patients in the nivolumab group and 49 (44%) patients in the placebo group. There were no treatment-related deaths in either group.

The most frequently reported grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events were diarrhoea (six [3%] of 221 in the nivolumab group vs two [2%] of 111 in the placebo group) and infusion-related reaction (six [3%] vs none).

strengths: Double-blind, placebo-controlled randomised phase III design
Included peritoneal as well as pleural mesothelioma
limitations: Placebo comparator rather than active chemotherapy
Patients were immunotherapy-naive; relevance after first-line immunotherapy is uncertain

clinicalImplications.text: Nivolumab improved PFS and OS over placebo in relapsed mesothelioma after platinum chemotherapy, supporting PD-1 blockade for immunotherapy-naive patients at relapse.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Most relevant for patients who did not receive first-line immunotherapy; patients already treated with nivolumab-ipilimumab were not studied.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 34656227.
